llm.summary: The skill's purpose (deploy a P2P Portal and run a local Bridge) is coherent with most requirements, but the package contains hard-coded secrets and workspace instructions that ask the agent to read and act on sensitive local files without explicit consent — the combination is risky and needs manual review before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to deploy a Portal to a VPS and run a local Bridge; required env vars (API key, hub URL, gateway URL, hooks token) and binaries (python3, ssh) match that purpose. However the repository also includes many workspace files (AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, etc.) that go beyond a single-skill scope and contain developer-specific secrets and deployment metadata that are not required for a clean, shareable skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md + included docs/scripts instruct the agent to read local OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, gateway.env) and memory files and to perform remote SSH operations and system configuration. AGENTS.md explicitly tells the agent to read MEMORY.md and other private files 'Before doing anything else' and to 'Don't ask permission. Just do it.' — this grants broad discretionary access to private data and encourages autonomous reading/exfiltration of local secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry-style install spec, but multiple scripts (auto_install.py, deploy scripts) perform remote git clone from a GitHub repo and run apt/pip, systemd and certbot via SSH. Pulling code from the referenced GitHub repo and running remote root-level installs is expected for a VPS deployment tool, but it still requires careful manual review because the repo included in the skill already contains many files with potentially sensitive content.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared env vars (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) are relevant. However the repository itself contains exposed secrets and host-specific info (hard-coded VPS IPs, admin password examples, API tokens in TOOLS.md and MEMORY.md). auto_install.py will attempt to auto-read local hooks token and write gateway.env — behavior that legitimately needs some secrets but also increases risk because the skill already contains clear examples of leaking sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill will write local configuration (~/.openclaw/gateway.env) and perform remote systemd/service setup on the VPS (expected for a Portal deploy). always=false (not force-included) which is appropriate. Still, scripts and docs encourage autonomous actions (automatic install, starting bridge, auto-reading config files) and AGENTS.md's 'do not ask' language increases the risk of the agent acting without adequate human confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill generally does what it says (deploy a Portal and run a local Bridge), but the package contains developer workspace files that include actual secrets (VPS IPs, API keys, admin passwords) and explicit instructions encouraging the agent to read local memory and config without asking. Before installing: 1) Do NOT provide your main SSH private key or unrestricted tokens — create a dedicated, limited SSH key and an account with minimal privileges. 2) Manually inspect and remove any hard-coded secrets in the skill repository (MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, AGENTS.md and similar). 3) Prefer manual deployment: run the deploy steps yourself on a disposable/testing VPS first rather than allowing the skill's auto_install to run. 4) If you must use auto-install, review auto_install.py and deploy scripts line-by-line and run them interactively (not blindly). 5) Rotate any tokens/keys that you expose during testing and restrict Hooks tokens. 6) Because the skill's source is 'unknown' / no homepage, be cautious — require the author to provide a canonical upstream repo and proof that the included workspace does not contain private credentials. If you are not comfortable auditing code or removing the embedded secrets, treat this skill as unsafe to install into a production/human workspace.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A pre-scan flagged base64-block pattern inside SKILL.md which can indicate embedded/obfuscated payloads or prompt-injection content. SKILL.md and many files are large and include automation scripts; this finding is not expected for a minimal deploy doc and warrants inspection of any encoded blocks.
